summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue in the setting of relapsed multiple myeloma and recent cytopenias. He had been receiving outpatient radiation for a perivesicular plasmacytoma, which had resolved his prior pain. Imaging showed mild bronchial wall thickening consistent with viral bronchitis, with no pneumonia. He was treated with intravenous and then oral levofloxacin, albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers, and supportive care. His respiratory symptoms improved, white blood cell count recovered, and he completed his prescribed radiation. He was discharged home with a two-week supply of nebulizers, a five-day course of oral antibiotics, and instructions to follow up with his oncology and primary care teams.
